claim: Clones of excitatory neurons derived from Nestin-positive progenitors labeled at embryonic day 10.5 are derived from two radial glia on average.
source: On average, individual clones contained two radial glia (median, range 1–4, Figure 1I and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Directly stated in the results section with supporting data from immunohistochemistry experiments at E12.5.

claim: Clones labeled at E10.5 span cortical layers 2–6.
source: Nearly all of the clones labeled at E10.5 in our study spanned cortical layers 2–6, consistent with prior studies labeling progenitors at this early developmental stage (Tan et al., 1998; Kaplan et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in the discussion section with citation to prior studies and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Clones labeled at E10.5 are composed of a random sampling of transcriptomic cell types.
source: The resulting clones are derived from two radial glia on average, span cortical layers 2–6, and are composed of a random sampling of transcriptomic cell types.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by transcriptomic analysis showing no bias in cell type composition between related and unrelated neurons.

claim: Related neurons are more likely to be connected vertically across cortical layers.
source: We find an interaction between shared lineage and connection type: related neurons are more likely to be connected vertically across cortical layers, but not laterally within the same layer.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological connectivity data showing increased vertical connection probability.

claim: Related neurons are not more likely to be connected laterally within the same layer.
source: We find an interaction between shared lineage and connection type: related neurons are more likely to be connected vertically across cortical layers, but not laterally within the same layer.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological connectivity data showing no difference in lateral connection probability.

claim: Tamoxifen administration at E9.5 resulted in clones containing on average 196 neurons (median).
source: Tamoxifen administration at E9.5 resulted in clones containing on average 196 neurons (median, interquartile range [IQR] 75–346 neurons) and spanning 347 μm in width (median, IQR 223–402 μm; Figure 1D,E).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data from clone reconstruction experiments.

claim: Tamoxifen administration at E10.5 resulted in clones containing on average 60 neurons (median).
source: Tamoxifen administration at E10.5 resulted in clones containing on average 60 neurons (median, IQR 26–117) and spanning 224 μm in width (median, IQR 140–298 μm; Figure 1D,E).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data from clone reconstruction experiments.

claim: Tamoxifen administration at E11.5 resulted in clones containing on average 39 neurons (median).
source: Tamoxifen administration at E11.5 resulted in clones containing on average 39 neurons (median, IQR 24–63) and spanning 220 μm in width (median, IQR 162–276 μm; Figure 1D,E), similar to the width of clones labeled at E10.5.
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data from clone reconstruction experiments.

claim: A substantial fraction of clones labeled at E11.5 did not contain neurons in the deep cortical layers 5–6 (20%).
source: However, a substantial fraction of clones labeled at E11.5 did not contain neurons in the deep cortical layers 5–6 (10/50 clones, 20%), which was only rarely seen in clones labeled by induction at E10.5 (1/39 clones, 3%), and never following induction at E9.5 (0/35 clones, 0%; (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data comparing different induction timepoints.

claim: The vast majority of clones labeled at E10.5 were arranged in a single proliferative unit (80%).
source: Although no well-accepted criteria are available for defining the boundaries of a proliferative unit, we found that the vast majority of our clones labeled at E10.5 were arranged in a single vertical track at E12.5 consistent with their belonging to a single proliferative unit (24 out of 30 clones, 80%, Figure 1J and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data from immunohistochemistry experiments.

claim: Tamoxifen administration at E10.5 labels predominantly individual radial glia and neuroepithelial stem cells in their final 1–2 cycles of symmetric cell division.
source: These findings show that tamoxifen administration at E10.5 labels predominantly individual radial glia and neuroepithelial stem cells in their final 1–2 cycles of symmetric cell division.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on immunohistochemistry data showing 1-4 radial glia per clone.

claim: Region-specific differences in gene expression are present in juvenile mouse neocortex between V1 and SS1.
source: Within L2/3 and L5, neurons from V1 and SS1 formed overlapping clusters in high-dimensional gene space (data not shown), but a cross-validated generalized linear model (GLM) could predict regional position slightly better than chance (Figure 2G,H), suggesting that L2/3 and L5 excitatory neurons in juvenile mouse neocortex have already begun differentiating along region-specific transcriptomic pathways.
evidence: Stated based on GLM analysis of transcriptomic data showing better-than-chance prediction of regional identity.

claim: Layer position and cortical region were the strongest predictors of transcriptomic variability among excitatory neurons.
source: Consistent with recent studies (Zeisel et al., 2015; Tasic et al., 2016; Tasic et al., 2018; Nowakowski et al., 2017), we found that layer position and cortical region were the strongest predictors of transcriptomic variability among excitatory neurons in our dataset (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated with citation to prior studies and supported by variance decomposition analysis.

claim: Pairs of related neurons were no more likely to map to the same broad transcriptomic class compared to pairs of nearby unrelated neurons.
source: Within individual clones, we found that pairs of related neurons were no more likely to map to the same broad transcriptomic class (p=0.71, Chi-squared test; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2), or specific cell type (p=0.70, Chi-squared test; Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2) compared to pairs of nearby unrelated neurons from the same cortical region.
evidence: Directly stated with statistical test results and figure references.

claim: Pairs of related neurons were no more likely to map to the same specific cell type compared to pairs of nearby unrelated neurons.
source: Within individual clones, we found that pairs of related neurons were no more likely to map to the same broad transcriptomic class (p=0.71, Chi-squared test; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2), or specific cell type (p=0.70, Chi-squared test; Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2) compared to pairs of nearby unrelated neurons from the same cortical region.
evidence: Directly stated with statistical test results and figure references.

claim: The L2/3 IT VISp Rrad transcriptomic cell type was underrepresented in labeled clones compared to unlabeled control neurons.
source: There was a difference in the overall distribution of labeled and unlabeled neurons among these thirteen cell types (p=0.039, Chi-squared test; Figure 3B), and post-hoc comparisons revealed that the L2/3 IT VISp Rrad transcriptomic cell type was underrepresented in our labeled clones compared to unlabeled control neurons (p=0.023, Chi-squared test with Bonferroni correction for 13 comparisons, Figure 3B; p>0.05 for the other 12 transcriptomic cell types).
evidence: Directly stated with statistical test results and figure references.

claim: Individual progenitors labeled at E10.5 give rise to a broad range of excitatory cell types.
source: While these findings cannot exclude the possibility of fate restriction of individual radial glia or intermediate progenitors labeled at later stages, they suggest that individual progenitors labeled at E10.5 give rise to a broad range of excitatory cell types.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the transcriptomic data showing diverse cell types within clones.

claim: 592 neurons (310 labeled and 282 unlabeled) from 86 clones in 43 mice were patched for connectivity experiments.
source: In total, we patched 592 neurons (310 labeled and 282 unlabeled) from 86 clones in 43 mice.
evidence: Directly stated as a summary of experimental data collection.

claim: 2049 potential excitatory connections were tested and 112 synaptic connections were identified.
source: In total, we tested 2049 potential excitatory connections and identified 112 synaptic connections.
evidence: Directly stated as a summary of connectivity testing results.

claim: The uEPSCs had a latency of 2.71 ± 1.06 ms (mean ± SD).
source: The uEPSCs had a latency of 2.71 ± 1.06 ms (n = 112 connections analyzed; mean ± SD), an amplitude of 12.83 ± 14.11 pA (n = 112 connections analyzed, mean ± SD), and were blocked by bath application of glutamatergic antagonists CNQX (20 μM) and APV (100 μM; uEPSC amplitude = 10.5 ± 5.4 pA and 0.0 ± 0.0 pA before and after the application of antagonists; median ±SE; n = 15 connections tested, p=6 × 10−5, Wilcoxon signed-rank test), further confirming that these were excitatory connections.
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative measurements from electrophysiology experiments.

claim: The uEPSCs had an amplitude of 12.83 ± 14.11 pA (mean ± SD).
source: The uEPSCs had a latency of 2.71 ± 1.06 ms (n = 112 connections analyzed; mean ± SD), an amplitude of 12.83 ± 14.11 pA (n = 112 connections analyzed, mean ± SD), and were blocked by bath application of glutamatergic antagonists CNQX (20 μM) and APV (100 μM; uEPSC amplitude = 10.5 ± 5.4 pA and 0.0 ± 0.0 pA before and after the application of antagonists; median ±SE; n = 15 connections tested, p=6 × 10−5, Wilcoxon signed-rank test), further confirming that these were excitatory connections.
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative measurements from electrophysiology experiments.

claim: uEPSCs were blocked by bath application of glutamatergic antagonists CNQX and APV.
source: The uEPSCs had a latency of 2.71 ± 1.06 ms (n = 112 connections analyzed; mean ± SD), an amplitude of 12.83 ± 14.11 pA (n = 112 connections analyzed, mean ± SD), and were blocked by bath application of glutamatergic antagonists CNQX (20 μM) and APV (100 μM; uEPSC amplitude = 10.5 ± 5.4 pA and 0.0 ± 0.0 pA before and after the application of antagonists; median ±SE; n = 15 connections tested, p=6 × 10−5, Wilcoxon signed-rank test), further confirming that these were excitatory connections.
evidence: Directly stated with statistical test results confirming the excitatory nature of connections.

claim: There was no evidence for a difference in overall connectivity between related and unrelated pairs (P=5.9% and P=5.2% for related and unrelated pairs, respectively; p=0.54).
source: Overall, there was no evidence for a difference in connectivity between related and unrelated pairs (P=5.9% and P=5.2% for related and unrelated pairs, respectively; p=0.54, Fisher's exact test; Figure 4D).
evidence: Directly stated with specific connection probabilities and statistical test results.

claim: Connection probability was increased between related pairs compared to unrelated pairs for vertical, across-layer connections (P=6.0% and P=2.7% for related and unrelated pairs, respectively; p=0.0056).
source: However, when we considered only connections linking cells vertically, across layers, we found that connection probability was increased between related pairs compared to unrelated pairs (P=6.0% and P=2.7% for related and unrelated pairs, respectively; p=0.0056, Fisher's exact test; Figure 4E), consistent with prior studies (Yu et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2012).
evidence: Directly stated with specific connection probabilities, statistical test results, and citations to prior studies.

claim: Connection probabilities from L4 to L5 were higher between related compared to unrelated pairs (P=11.3% and P=2.3% for related and unrelated pairs, respectively; p=0.033).
source: At the level of layer-specific connection types, we found that the connection probabilities from L4 to L5 (P=11.3% and P=2.3% for related and unrelated pairs, respectively; p=0.033, Fisher's exact test; Figure 4F) and from L2/3 to L5 (P=7.9% and P=1.6%, for related and unrelated pairs respectively; p=0.056, Fisher's exact test; Figure 4F) were higher between related compared to unrelated pairs.
evidence: Directly stated with specific connection probabilities and statistical test results.

claim: Connection probabilities from L2/3 to L5 were higher between related compared to unrelated pairs (P=7.9% and P=1.6%, for related and unrelated pairs respectively; p=0.056).
source: At the level of layer-specific connection types, we found that the connection probabilities from L4 to L5 (P=11.3% and P=2.3% for related and unrelated pairs, respectively; p=0.033, Fisher's exact test; Figure 4F) and from L2/3 to L5 (P=7.9% and P=1.6%, for related and unrelated pairs respectively; p=0.056, Fisher's exact test; Figure 4F) were higher between related compared to unrelated pairs.
evidence: Directly stated with specific connection probabilities and statistical test results.

claim: There was no evidence for an increase in lateral connections within the same cortical layer between related neurons compared to unrelated neurons (P=5.6% and P=8.1% for related and unrelated pairs, respectively; p=0.25).
source: In contrast to vertical connections, we did not find evidence for an increase in the number of lateral connections within the same cortical layer between related neurons compared to unrelated neurons (P=5.6% and P=8.1% for related and unrelated pairs, respectively; p=0.25, Fisher's exact test; Figure 5A–C).
evidence: Directly stated with specific connection probabilities and statistical test results.

claim: There was no statistically significant difference in bidirectional lateral connections between related and unrelated pairs (P=0% for related lateral pairs and P=2.1% for unrelated lateral pairs; p=0.19).
source: There was also no statistically significant difference in bidirectional lateral connections between related and unrelated pairs (P=0% for related lateral pairs and P=2.1% for unrelated lateral pairs in which both directions of connectivity were tested; p=0.19, Fisher's exact test; Figure 5C).
evidence: Directly stated with specific connection probabilities and statistical test results.

claim: The study had approximately 97% statistical power to detect an increase in lateral connectivity of the same magnitude as found for vertical connectivity.
source: We found that, if we assume that the increase in connectivity among neurons derived from a single radial glial cell is the same for vertical and lateral connections, and that there are two radial glial lineages per clone, we had approximately 97% statistical power to detect an increase in lateral connectivity of the same magnitude as we found for vertical connectivity (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Directly stated based on power analysis calculations.

claim: The generalized linear model revealed a significant interaction between cell lineage and connection type (p=0.035).
source: The model revealed a significant interaction between cell lineage and connection type (p=0.035), further supporting that the effect of cell lineage on connectivity depends on the type of connection tested.
evidence: Directly stated with statistical test results from GLM analysis.

claim: The model revealed a weak decrease in connection probability with Euclidean distance for lateral connections (p=0.056).
source: The model also revealed a weak decrease in connection probability with Euclidean distance for lateral connections (p=0.056) and no evidence for any influence of rostro-caudal position (p>0.5 for the main effect and all interactions).
evidence: Directly stated with statistical test results from GLM analysis.

claim: There was no evidence for any influence of rostro-caudal position on connection probability (p>0.5 for the main effect and all interactions).
source: The model also revealed a weak decrease in connection probability with Euclidean distance for lateral connections (p=0.056) and no evidence for any influence of rostro-caudal position (p>0.5 for the main effect and all interactions).
evidence: Directly stated with statistical test results from GLM analysis.

claim: Integration of vertical intra-clonal input with lateral inter-clonal input may represent a developmentally programmed connectivity motif supporting the emergence of functional circuits.
source: These findings challenge the view that related neurons show uniformly increased connectivity and suggest that integration of vertical intra-clonal input with lateral inter-clonal input may represent a developmentally programmed connectivity motif supporting the emergence of functional circuits.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as an interpretation of the connectivity findings.

claim: Clonally related excitatory neurons are more likely to be synaptically connected has been reported in prior studies using retroviral lineage tracing.
source: A series of studies using a retroviral lineage tracing method has suggested that clonally related excitatory neurons are more likely to be synaptically connected to each other (Yu et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2012; He et al., 2015) and have similar preferred orientations in primary visual cortex (V1) compared to unrelated neurons (Li et al., 2012), providing support for the long-standing hypothesis that radial clones may constitute elementary circuit modules for information processing in the cortex (Rakic, 1988; Mountcastle, 1997; Buxhoeveden and Casanova, 2002).
evidence: Stated with multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: Clonally related neurons have similar preferred orientations in primary visual cortex compared to unrelated neurons.
source: A series of studies using a retroviral lineage tracing method has suggested that clonally related excitatory neurons are more likely to be synaptically connected to each other (Yu et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2012; He et al., 2015) and have similar preferred orientations in primary visual cortex (V1) compared to unrelated neurons (Li et al., 2012), providing support for the long-standing hypothesis that radial clones may constitute elementary circuit modules for information processing in the cortex (Rakic, 1988; Mountcastle, 1997; Buxhoeveden and Casanova, 2002).
evidence: Stated with citation to prior study.

claim: Radial clones may constitute elementary circuit modules for information processing in the cortex.
source: A series of studies using a retroviral lineage tracing method has suggested that clonally related excitatory neurons are more likely to be synaptically connected to each other (Yu et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2012; He et al., 2015) and have similar preferred orientations in primary visual cortex (V1) compared to unrelated neurons (Li et al., 2012), providing support for the long-standing hypothesis that radial clones may constitute elementary circuit modules for information processing in the cortex (Rakic, 1988; Mountcastle, 1997; Buxhoeveden and Casanova, 2002).
evidence: Stated as a long-standing hypothesis with citations to foundational papers.

claim: Cortical neurogenesis lasts from approximately embryonic day 10.5 (E10.5) through E17.5 in the mouse.
source: During cortical neurogenesis, which lasts from approximately embryonic day 10.5 (E10.5) through E17.5 in the mouse (Caviness et al., 1995; Takahashi et al., 1996), radial glial cells undergo asymmetric division to generate postmitotic excitatory neurons that migrate radially to populate the cortical plate.
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies establishing the timeline of neurogenesis.

claim: Radial glial cells undergo asymmetric division to generate postmitotic excitatory neurons that migrate radially to populate the cortical plate.
source: During cortical neurogenesis, which lasts from approximately embryonic day 10.5 (E10.5) through E17.5 in the mouse (Caviness et al., 1995; Takahashi et al., 1996), radial glial cells undergo asymmetric division to generate postmitotic excitatory neurons that migrate radially to populate the cortical plate.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about cortical development.

claim: Neurogenesis occurs in an inside-out gradient, such that early born neurons occupy the deep cortical layers and later-born neurons reside in progressively more superficial layers.
source: Neurogenesis occurs in an inside-out gradient, such that early born neurons occupy the deep cortical layers and later-born neurons reside in progressively more superficial layers (Angevine and Sidman, 1961; Rakic, 1974; Caviness et al., 1995).
evidence: Stated with citations to foundational studies establishing the inside-out pattern of cortical development.

claim: The ventricular zone is subdivided by glial septa into well-defined columns of precursor or stem cells referred to as 'proliferative units'.
source: The ventricular zone is subdivided by glial septa into well-defined columns of precursor or stem cells referred to as 'proliferative units' that give rise to a radial unit of clonally related excitatory neurons, sometimes referred to as an ontogenetic column (Torii et al., 2009; Kriegstein and Noctor, 2004; Noctor et al., 2001; Noctor et al., 2007; Rakic, 1988).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies describing the organization of the ventricular zone.

claim: Radial units of clonally related neurons are only loosely clustered and are heavily intermixed with numerous nearby unrelated neurons.
source: However, these radial units of clonally related neurons are only loosely clustered and are heavily intermixed with numerous nearby unrelated neurons (Walsh and Cepko, 1988; Tan et al., 1995) and there is substantial tangential migration of clonally related neurons as they traverse the subventricular zone and intermediate zone en route to the developing cortical plate (Torii et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies showing the dispersion of clonally related neurons.

claim: There is substantial tangential migration of clonally related neurons as they traverse the subventricular zone and intermediate zone en route to the developing cortical plate.
source: However, these radial units of clonally related neurons are only loosely clustered and are heavily intermixed with numerous nearby unrelated neurons (Walsh and Cepko, 1988; Tan et al., 1995) and there is substantial tangential migration of clonally related neurons as they traverse the subventricular zone and intermediate zone en route to the developing cortical plate (Torii et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated with citation to prior study.

claim: Inhibitory interneurons are generated in the ganglionic eminences and migrate tangentially to disperse throughout the developing cortical mantle.
source: In contrast to excitatory neurons, inhibitory interneurons are generated in the ganglionic eminences and migrate tangentially to disperse throughout the developing cortical mantle (Letinic et al., 2002; Kriegstein and Noctor, 2004; Tan et al., 1998; Mayer et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies establishing the origin and migration of interneurons.

claim: Excitatory neurons in the adult mouse cortex are largely region-specific at the level of transcriptomic cell types.
source: In contrast to inhibitory interneurons, excitatory neurons in the adult mouse (Tasic et al., 2018) and developing human (Nowakowski et al., 2017) cortex are largely region-specific at the level of transcriptomic cell types, with several dozens of excitatory cell types per area (Tasic et al., 2018; Hodge et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated with citations to recent transcriptomic studies.

claim: The vast majority of cells within radial clones are excitatory neurons.
source: While it is well-established that the vast majority of cells within radial clones are excitatory neurons (Tan et al., 1998), it remains controversial whether individual progenitors give rise to the full diversity of excitatory neuron cell types within a given cortical area, or only to a restricted subset of transcriptomic cell types (Franco et al., 2012; Gil-Sanz et al., 2015; Eckler et al., 2015; Kaplan et al., 2017; Llorca et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated as well-established knowledge with citation.

claim: It remains controversial whether individual progenitors give rise to the full diversity of excitatory neuron cell types within a given cortical area, or only to a restricted subset of transcriptomic cell types.
source: While it is well-established that the vast majority of cells within radial clones are excitatory neurons (Tan et al., 1998), it remains controversial whether individual progenitors give rise to the full diversity of excitatory neuron cell types within a given cortical area, or only to a restricted subset of transcriptomic cell types (Franco et al., 2012; Gil-Sanz et al., 2015; Eckler et al., 2015; Kaplan et al., 2017; Llorca et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated as an ongoing controversy with citations to conflicting studies.

claim: Gap junction coupling during migration along the same radial glial fiber is thought to be involved in the mechanism by which translaminar clones form specific connections.
source: The mechanism by which translaminar clones of excitatory neurons form specific connections is thought to involve gap junction coupling during migration along the same radial glial fiber (Yu et al., 2012; He et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies proposing this mechanism.

claim: It is the coupling between clonally related neurons, and not between the postmitotic neurons and their radial glia, that promotes specific synapse formation between radially aligned sister neurons.
source: A recent study has further shown that it is the coupling between clonally related neurons, and not between the postmitotic neurons and their radial glia, that promotes specific synapse formation between radially aligned sister neurons (He et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated with citation to a specific study.

claim: Coupling between clonally related neurons requires the inside-out migration of related neurons along a similar path and is abolished by removal of REELIN or its downstream effector DAB1.
source: Furthermore, this coupling requires the inside-out migration of related neurons along a similar path and is abolished by removal of REELIN or its downstream effector DAB1 (He et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated with citation to a specific study.

claim: Connections from L2/3 to L5 and from L4 to L5 are most strongly enhanced between clonally related neurons.
source: Our finding that connections from L2/3 to L5 and from L4 to L5 are most strongly enhanced between clonally related neurons is consistent with a mechanism that requires inside-out migration along a radial glial fiber and further suggests that as migrating neurons travel to reach the more superficial layers, their axons may somehow 'stick' to the maturing apical dendrites of the deep layer neurons they are passing.
evidence: Stated as a finding with mechanistic speculation.

claim: Even distantly related neurons that are in close physical proximity and migrate along the same radial glial pathway may be predisposed to develop vertical connections with one another.
source: Furthermore, our findings suggest that even distantly related neurons that are in close physical proximity and migrate along the same radial glial pathway may be predisposed to develop vertical connections with one another, and not just closely related neurons derived from the same radial glial cell.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the connectivity findings.

claim: Migration of clonally related neurons along multiple radial glial fibers may be quite common, resulting in substantial tangential dispersion that requires EphA/Ephrin-A signaling during neuronal migration.
source: Interestingly, early studies in the rat suggested that migration of clonally related neurons along multiple radial glial fibers may be quite common (Walsh and Cepko, 1988), resulting in substantial tangential dispersion that requires EphA/Ephrin-A signaling during neuronal migration (Torii et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: Expression of specific cell adhesion molecules may play a role in promoting vertical connections and/or repelling lateral connections among clonally related neurons.
source: Expression of specific cell adhesion molecules may also play a role in promoting vertical connections and/or repelling lateral connections among clonally related neurons (Tarusawa et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated as a possibility with citation to a prior study.

claim: L5 serves as a major output of the cortex with important roles in integrating feedback from higher cortical areas and in top-down modulation by brain states.
source: Neurons in L5 serve as a major output of the cortex with important roles in integrating feedback from higher cortical areas and in top-down modulation by brain states (Kim et al., 2015), and altered gene expression in deep layer neurons during midfetal development has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders such as autism (Willsey et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: Altered gene expression in deep layer neurons during midfetal development has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders such as autism.
source: Neurons in L5 serve as a major output of the cortex with important roles in integrating feedback from higher cortical areas and in top-down modulation by brain states (Kim et al., 2015), and altered gene expression in deep layer neurons during midfetal development has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders such as autism (Willsey et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated with citation to a prior study.

claim: Integration of translaminar input from related neurons with intralaminar input from unrelated neurons in L5 may represent an organizing principle of lineage-associated circuit assembly.
source: Our data suggest that integration of translaminar input from related neurons with intralaminar input from unrelated neurons in L5 may represent an organizing principle of lineage-associated circuit assembly.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the connectivity findings.

claim: The prevailing view has been that preferential connectivity between clonally related excitatory neurons mirrors that of the canonical cortical circuit.
source: These findings argue against the prevailing view that preferential connectivity between clonally related excitatory neurons mirrors that of the canonical cortical circuit, and suggest that integration of vertical input from related neurons with lateral inputs from unrelated neurons may represent a developmentally programmed motif for assembling functional cortical circuits.
evidence: Stated as the prevailing view that the current findings challenge.

claim: The findings challenge the view that related neurons show uniformly increased connectivity.
source: These findings challenge the view that related neurons show uniformly increased connectivity and suggest that integration of vertical intra-clonal input with lateral inter-clonal input may represent a developmentally programmed connectivity motif supporting the emergence of functional circuits.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a key conclusion.

claim: The assumption that all local connections are uniformly increased between clonally related excitatory neurons has become dogma in the field.
source: Therefore, it remains unclear whether all local connections are uniformly increased between clonally related excitatory neurons, although this assumption has become dogma in the field (Li et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated with citation to a review article.

claim: A direct comparison of related and unrelated pairs for each layer-specific connection type was not done in prior studies.
source: The projection pattern of vertical, across-layer connections between related neurons was qualitatively similar to the canonical circuit of layer-specific connections in adult cortex (Yu et al., 2009); however, a direct comparison of related and unrelated pairs for each layer-specific connection type was not done, and lateral connections between clonally related cells within the same cortical layer were not examined.
evidence: Stated as a gap in prior research with citation.

claim: Lateral connections between clonally related cells within the same cortical layer were not examined in prior studies.
source: The projection pattern of vertical, across-layer connections between related neurons was qualitatively similar to the canonical circuit of layer-specific connections in adult cortex (Yu et al., 2009); however, a direct comparison of related and unrelated pairs for each layer-specific connection type was not done, and lateral connections between clonally related cells within the same cortical layer were not examined.
evidence: Stated as a gap in prior research with citation.

claim: The difficulty of multi-patching experiments combined with relatively low connectivity rates between excitatory neurons necessitate testing a very large number of connections.
source: The difficulty of multi-patching experiments combined with the relatively low connectivity rates between excitatory neurons (Jiang et al., 2015; Markram et al., 1997; Barth et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2016) necessitate testing a very large number of connections and pose an enormous technical challenge to fully answer this question.
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies documenting low connectivity rates.

claim: Using an enhancer trap Cre line to label neural progenitors at an earlier developmental stage yields much larger clones (approximately 670–800 neurons per clone compared to 4–6 neurons per clone with retroviral labeling at E12.5).
source: Using an enhancer trap Cre line to label neural progenitors at an earlier developmental stage, yielding much larger clones (approximately 670–800 neurons per clone compared to 4–6 neurons per clone in Yu et al., 2009), a separate group has also reported an association between shared lineage and orientation tuning in V1 (Ohtsuki et al., 2012), although with a much smaller effect size than reported in Li et al. (2012) for small clones.
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies comparing clone sizes.

claim: A study examining lateral connections within layer 4 of large clones labeled in chimeric mice at approximately E3.5 found transient increases in connectivity between clonally related cells.
source: Another study examined lateral connections within layer 4 (L4) of large clones labeled in chimeric mice at approximately E3.5 (Tarusawa et al., 2016) and found transient increases in connectivity between clonally related cells.
evidence: Stated with citation to a prior study.

claim: The relationship between lineage and the layer-specific connectivity matrix has not been systematically studied in large clones.
source: However, the relationship between lineage and the layer-specific connectivity matrix has not been systematically studied in large clones, and there remains a major disconnect in scale between studies of lineage-associated connectivity and the development of larger, functional cortical units that are thought to implement computations.
evidence: Stated as a gap in the literature.

claim: Nestin is expressed by neuroepithelial stem cells and ventricular radial glia.
source: Given that Nestin is expressed by neuroepithelial stem cells and ventricular radial glia (Hockfield and McKay, 1985; Misson et al., 1988) and that the transition between neuroepithelial stem cells and radial glia occurs between E10.25 and E11.5 (Misson et al., 1988; Anthony et al., 2004; Nowakowski et al., 2011), it is possible that a subset of our clones are derived from neuroepithelial stem cells.
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: The transition between neuroepithelial stem cells and radial glia occurs between E10.25 and E11.5.
source: Given that Nestin is expressed by neuroepithelial stem cells and ventricular radial glia (Hockfield and McKay, 1985; Misson et al., 1988) and that the transition between neuroepithelial stem cells and radial glia occurs between E10.25 and E11.5 (Misson et al., 1988; Anthony et al., 2004; Nowakowski et al., 2011), it is possible that a subset of our clones are derived from neuroepithelial stem cells.
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: There is a substantial delay in onset and prolonged pharmacokinetic activity of tamoxifen following oral administration.
source: However, there is a substantial delay in onset and prolonged pharmacokinetic activity of tamoxifen following oral administration (Robinson et al., 1991), and an inherent imprecision in the timing of pregnancies.
evidence: Stated with citation to a prior study.

claim: Pax6 is expressed in radial glial and intermediate progenitors.
source: embryos were sacrificed at E12.5 following tamoxifen administration at E10.5 and immunohistochemistry for Pax6 (expressed in radial glial and intermediate progenitors, Götz et al., 1998) and Tbr2 (also known as Eomes, a marker of intermediate progenitors, Englund et al., 2005; Mihalas et al., 2016) were performed to characterize the type and number of progenitors within individual clones (Figure 1G,H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).

claim: Proliferative units can be identified as well-defined columns of precursor or stem cells within the ventricular zone.
source: As described by Rakic (1988), proliferative units can be identified as well-defined columns of precursor or stem cells within the ventricular zone; it has been proposed that the polyclonal precursors within a proliferative unit collectively give rise to a population of postmitotic neurons that share a common radial glial scaffold and form a morphologically identifiable stack of neurons in the cortex termed an 'ontogenetic' or 'embryonic' column (Rakic, 1988).
evidence: Stated with citation to Rakic's foundational work.

claim: The polyclonal precursors within a proliferative unit collectively give rise to a population of postmitotic neurons that share a common radial glial scaffold and form a morphologically identifiable stack of neurons in the cortex termed an 'ontogenetic' or 'embryonic' column.

evidence: Stated with citation to Rakic's foundational work.

claim: Different cortical areas are composed of distinct transcriptomic excitatory neuron cell types in adult mouse neocortex.
source: Recent transcriptomic cell atlases of adult mouse neocortex showed that different cortical areas are composed of distinct transcriptomic excitatory neuron cell types (Tasic et al., 2018; Saunders et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated with citations to recent transcriptomic studies.

claim: 206 neurons were analyzed after quality control for single-cell RNA-sequencing.
source: We analyzed 206 neurons (after quality control, see Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Methods) which had approximately 0.36 million uniquely mapping reads (median; IQR 0.17–0.69 million reads; Figure 2C) and approximately 7000 genes detected (median: 7007; IQR 6152–7920 genes; Figure 2D) on average per cell.
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data.

claim: Most neurons patched in L4 mapped to L4 reference types (68.2%).

claim: Cells from both V1 and SS1 mapped predominantly to V1 excitatory neuron types (94.9% of V1 cells and 92.4% of SS1 cells).
source: Area SS1 was not specifically profiled in the reference cell atlas; we found that cells from both V1 and SS1 in our dataset mapped predominantly to V1 excitatory neuron types (94.9% of V1 cells and 92.4% of SS1 cells; Figure 3—source data 1) with only a handful mapping to ALM excitatory neuron types (3.4% of V1 cells and 3.8% of SS1 cells).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data from mapping analysis.

claim: The quality of the mapping was equally good for V1 and SS1 cells (correlations to best matching cluster for SS1 cells, 0.78 ± 0.08; for V1 cells, 0.78 ± 0.07; p=0.76).
source: Of note, the quality of the mapping was equally good for V1 and SS1 cells (correlations to best matching cluster for SS1 cells, 0.78 ± 0.08; for V1 cells, 0.78 ± 0.07; mean ± SD; p=0.76, two-sample t-test), suggesting that the adult V1/ALM cell type atlas is an equally reasonable reference for excitatory neurons in juvenile V1 and SS1.
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data and statistical test results.

claim: The adult V1/ALM cell type atlas is an equally reasonable reference for excitatory neurons in juvenile V1 and SS1.
source: Of note, the quality of the mapping was equally good for V1 and SS1 cells (correlations to best matching cluster for SS1 cells, 0.78 ± 0.08; for V1 cells, 0.78 ± 0.07; mean ± SD; p=0.76, two-sample t-test), suggesting that the adult V1/ALM cell type atlas is an equally reasonable reference for excitatory neurons in juvenile V1 and SS1.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the mapping quality data.

claim: The progenitors labeled in the study collectively give rise to the majority of transcriptomic cell types present in the areas of cortex examined.
source: These findings demonstrate that the progenitors labeled in our study collectively give rise to the majority of transcriptomic cell types present in the areas of cortex examined, but suggest that the L2/3 IT VISp Rrad transcriptomic cell type may arise from a distinct progenitor pool.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the transcriptomic mapping data.

claim: The L2/3 IT VISp Rrad transcriptomic cell type may arise from a distinct progenitor pool.
source: These findings demonstrate that the progenitors labeled in our study collectively give rise to the majority of transcriptomic cell types present in the areas of cortex examined, but suggest that the L2/3 IT VISp Rrad transcriptomic cell type may arise from a distinct progenitor pool.
evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on the underrepresentation of this cell type in labeled clones.

claim: A single bidirectional connection was identified between related neurons (1/324, P=0.31%).
source: A single bidirectional connection was identified between related neurons (1/324, P=0.31%), and six were identified between unrelated neurons (6/617, P=0.97%; p=0.43, Fisher's exact test, Figure 4D).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data.

claim: Six bidirectional connections were identified between unrelated neurons (6/617, P=0.97%).
source: A single bidirectional connection was identified between related neurons (1/324, P=0.31%), and six were identified between unrelated neurons (6/617, P=0.97%; p=0.43, Fisher's exact test, Figure 4D).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data.

claim: A single vertical bidirectional connection was identified between related neurons (P=0.47%).
source: A single vertical bidirectional connection was identified between related neurons (P=0.47%), and none were identified between unrelated neurons (P=0.0%; p=0.39, Fisher's exact test; Figure 4E).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data.

claim: No vertical bidirectional connections were identified between unrelated neurons (P=0.0%).
source: A single vertical bidirectional connection was identified between related neurons (P=0.47%), and none were identified between unrelated neurons (P=0.0%; p=0.39, Fisher's exact test; Figure 4E).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative data.

claim: The vertical connection probability between neurons derived from a single radial glial cell would be estimated to be approximately P=9.4%.
source: If we assume that only a shared radial glial lineage predisposes cells to be synaptically connected, and given that we had on average N = 2 radial glial progenitors per clone (Figure 1G–I), then the vertical connection probability between neurons derived from a single radial glial cell would be estimated to be even higher (approximately P=9.4%) in order to yield the P=6.0% vertical connectivity that we found among clonally related cells (see Methods).
evidence: Stated as a calculation based on the observed data and assumptions about clone composition.

claim: Using previously reported connection probabilities and a clone size of 6 neurons, the model predicts that only 1.9 ± 0.5% of the total input to a cell comes from its sister cells.
source: If we fit the model using previously reported connection probabilities (P=36.3%, 65/179, for related pairs; P=6.3%, 9/143, for unrelated pairs; Yu et al., 2009 Figure 3H, pooling connections tested across control groups) and assume a clone size of 6 neurons using the retroviral lineage tracing method with labeling at E12.5 (Yu et al., 2009), the model predicts that, despite the very high connection probability between closely related 'sister' cells, only a small fraction of the total input to a cell comes from its sister cells (1.9 ± 0.5%, mean ± SEM, Figure 4G).
evidence: Stated as a model prediction based on prior data with citation.

claim: Using empirically measured connection probabilities and clone size (60 neurons on average), the model estimates that 5.0 ± 1.8% of L4→L2/3 connections originate from cells with a common developmental lineage.
source: Indeed, using our empirically measured connection probabilities and clone size (60 neurons on average), the model estimates that a larger fraction of inputs from L4 to L2/3, L4 to L5, and L2/3 to L5 originates from cells with a common developmental lineage (5.0 ± 1.8% of L4→L2/3 connections, 14.0 ± 9.5% of L4→L5 connections, and 13.6 ± 9.4% of L2/3→L5 connections; estimate ± SE, Figure 4G).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative estimates from the connectivity model.

claim: Using empirically measured connection probabilities and clone size (60 neurons on average), the model estimates that 14.0 ± 9.5% of L4→L5 connections originate from cells with a common developmental lineage.
source: Indeed, using our empirically measured connection probabilities and clone size (60 neurons on average), the model estimates that a larger fraction of inputs from L4 to L2/3, L4 to L5, and L2/3 to L5 originates from cells with a common developmental lineage (5.0 ± 1.8% of L4→L2/3 connections, 14.0 ± 9.5% of L4→L5 connections, and 13.6 ± 9.4% of L2/3→L5 connections; estimate ± SE, Figure 4G).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative estimates from the connectivity model.

claim: Using empirically measured connection probabilities and clone size (60 neurons on average), the model estimates that 13.6 ± 9.4% of L2/3→L5 connections originate from cells with a common developmental lineage.
source: Indeed, using our empirically measured connection probabilities and clone size (60 neurons on average), the model estimates that a larger fraction of inputs from L4 to L2/3, L4 to L5, and L2/3 to L5 originates from cells with a common developmental lineage (5.0 ± 1.8% of L4→L2/3 connections, 14.0 ± 9.5% of L4→L5 connections, and 13.6 ± 9.4% of L2/3→L5 connections; estimate ± SE, Figure 4G).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative estimates from the connectivity model.

claim: Certain layer-specific, vertical connections show a stronger contribution of lineage-associated connections than expected based on previous data.
source: These findings show that certain layer-specific, vertical connections show a stronger contribution of lineage-associated connections than expected based on previous data, and suggest that even distantly related cells derived from multiple radial glia develop preferential connectivity, possibly as a result of physical proximity during neurogenesis and/or a common migratory route.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the connectivity model estimates.

claim: Even distantly related cells derived from multiple radial glia develop preferential connectivity, possibly as a result of physical proximity during neurogenesis and/or a common migratory route.
source: These findings show that certain layer-specific, vertical connections show a stronger contribution of lineage-associated connections than expected based on previous data, and suggest that even distantly related cells derived from multiple radial glia develop preferential connectivity, possibly as a result of physical proximity during neurogenesis and/or a common migratory route.
evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on the connectivity findings.

claim: The connectivity model estimates that only 1.0 ± 0.8% of connections within L2/3 come from related neurons.
source: Our connectivity model estimates that only a small fraction of lateral, within-layer input to a cell comes from related neurons (1.0 ± 0.8% of connections within L2/3, 3.0 ± 1.1% of connections within L4, and 0.7 ± 0.7% of connections within L5; estimate ± SE; Figure 5E).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative estimates from the connectivity model.

claim: The connectivity model estimates that 3.0 ± 1.1% of connections within L4 come from related neurons.
source: Our connectivity model estimates that only a small fraction of lateral, within-layer input to a cell comes from related neurons (1.0 ± 0.8% of connections within L2/3, 3.0 ± 1.1% of connections within L4, and 0.7 ± 0.7% of connections within L5; estimate ± SE; Figure 5E).
evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative estimates from the connectivity model.

claim: The connectivity model estimates that 0.7 ± 0.7% of connections within L5 come from related neurons.

evidence: Directly stated with specific quantitative estimates from the connectivity model.

claim: Clonally related neurons are not preferentially connected to each other within a cortical layer, even if one considers only neurons derived from the same radial glial cell as meaningfully 'related'.
source: Therefore, these data convincingly show that clonally related neurons are not preferentially connected to each other within a cortical layer, even if one considers only neurons derived from the same radial glial cell as meaningfully 'related'.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the connectivity data and power analysis.

claim: The findings suggest a revised model of lineage-associated synaptic connectivity that is connection type-specific, with related cells preferentially connected vertically, across cortical layers, but not laterally within the same layer.
source: These findings suggest a revised model of lineage-associated synaptic connectivity that is connection type-specific, with related cells preferentially connected vertically, across cortical layers, but not laterally within the same layer (Figure 5F).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the connectivity findings.

claim: Connection probability depends on the distance between cells.
source: Since connection probability also depends on the distance between cells (Perin et al., 2011; Ko et al., 2011), and potentially on cortical area, we performed additional analyses in order to take these variables into account.
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: Excitatory neurons in L2/3 with similar orientation tuning are more likely to be synaptically connected and have stronger synapses compared to cells with dissimilar tuning preferences.
source: Several studies have shown that excitatory neurons in L2/3 with similar orientation tuning are more likely to be synaptically connected and have stronger synapses compared to cells with dissimilar tuning preferences (Ko et al., 2011; Cossell et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: An alternate mechanism such as common input from L4, from nearby unrelated neurons, or from long-range feedback connections may drive similarity in orientation tuning preferences between clonally related neurons in L2/3.
source: However, we found no increase in lateral connections between related cells in L2/3, suggesting that an alternate mechanism such as common input from L4, from nearby unrelated neurons, or from long-range feedback connections may drive their similarity in orientation tuning preferences.
evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on the lack of increased lateral connectivity.

claim: The findings suggest a novel functional role of lateral connections within L2/3 in facilitating communication between adjacent developmental clones.
source: These results suggest a novel functional role of lateral connections within L2/3 in facilitating communication between adjacent developmental clones.
evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on the connectivity findings.

claim: L5 is highlighted as a potential hub within translaminar clones, with the most striking increases in connectivity seen in the projections from layers L2/3 and L4 to L5.
source: Our results highlight L5 as a potential hub within translaminar clones, with the most striking increases in connectivity seen in the projections from layers L2/3 and L4 to L5.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the connectivity findings.

claim: It is possible that clonally related neurons residing in the same layer are derived from the same intermediate progenitor cell, and that this close lineage relationship confers an additional reduction in connectivity.
source: For example, it is possible that clonally related neurons residing in the same layer are derived from the same intermediate progenitor cell, and that this close lineage relationship confers an additional reduction in connectivity (Ellender et al., 2019) which is not inherited by neurons in other layers derived from the same radial glial cell.
evidence: Stated as a possibility with citation to a prior study.

claim: L6 neurons undergo nuclear translocation, whereby they attach their leading process directly to the pial surface, rather than locomoting along a radial glial fiber.
source: Layer six neurons were not included in our study for two main reasons: 1) L6 neurons undergo nuclear translocation, whereby they attach their leading process directly to the pial surface, rather than locomoting along a radial glial fiber (Gupta et al., 2002) and therefore may be less likely to show radial glial fiber-dependent connectivity
evidence: Stated with citation to a prior study.

claim: Including L6 in the study would have disproportionately increased the number of possible connection types from 9 to 16.
source: and 2) including an additional layer in our study would have disproportionately increased the number of possible connection types we needed to test (from 9 to 16), making the task experimentally impractical.
evidence: Stated as a practical consideration for experimental design.

claim: The statistical power to detect a 50% decrease in connectivity is approximately 16%.
source: Of note, while we are well-powered to detect an increase in connectivity, our statistical power to detect a decrease in connectivity is substantially lower due to the overall low connectivity rate among excitatory neurons (we estimate a 16% probability of detecting a 50% decrease in connectivity, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Directly stated based on power analysis calculations.

claim: The data cannot exclude the possibility that lateral connectivity is actually decreased between clonally related neurons.
source: Thus, our data cannot exclude the possibility that lateral connectivity is actually decreased between clonally related neurons.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of the study based on statistical power.

claim: Transcriptomic cell type correlates with the long-range projection pattern of excitatory neurons.
source: Our acute slice preparation only allows us to test local connections; however, given that transcriptomic cell type correlates with the long-range projection pattern of excitatory neurons (Tasic et al., 2018), our finding that individual clones contain multiple diverse transcriptomic types suggests that they also project to diverse targets.
evidence: Stated with citation to a prior study.

claim: Individual clones contain multiple diverse transcriptomic types, suggesting that they also project to diverse targets.
source: Our acute slice preparation only allows us to test local connections; however, given that transcriptomic cell type correlates with the long-range projection pattern of excitatory neurons (Tasic et al., 2018), our finding that individual clones contain multiple diverse transcriptomic types suggests that they also project to diverse targets.
evidence: Stated as an inference based on the transcriptomic diversity within clones.

claim: Integration of feedforward, intra-clonal input with lateral, inter-clonal information may represent a developmentally programmed connectivity motif for the assembly of neocortical circuits.
source: However, our data suggest that the integration of feedforward, intra-clonal input with lateral, inter-clonal information may represent a developmentally programmed connectivity motif for the assembly of neocortical circuits.
evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on the connectivity findings.
